text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Thursday.

GERMANY - Bund futures ended slightly lower with several large British accounts selling late in the day. German data dashed hopes of a rate cut. U.S. jobs figures released on Friday are now in focus. The June Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 101.67, down 0.13 from Wednesday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - British short sterling futures were the main beneficiaries after a survey by the Confederation of British Industry showing that sales growth was slowing. The June long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 111-13/32, up 02/32 from Wednesday's settlement price.

FRANCE - Bond futures never really recovered from a weak start after a spate of short selling on GLOBEX. They survived tests of support close to 131, however, prompting some traders to say the worst of the falls was over. The March notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 131.28, down 0.26 from Wednesday's settlement price.

ITALY - The debt market saw timid positive signals with the June Bpt Liffe future ending firmer but off session highs, but a mood of caution prevailed. The June bond future on LIFFE was trading at 127.12, up 0.63 from Wednesday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - The prices of U.S. government securities opened flat to higher as the market maintained gains scored after Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan said nothing further to spook financial markets on Wednesday. The June Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 109-27/32, down 03/32 from Wednesday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.85 percent.

JAPAN - The key June 10-year Japanese government bond futures contract closed sharply higher as an unexpected rise caused dealers' short-squeezing. In after hours trading the June future on LIFFE was trading at 125.39, up 0.45 from Wednesday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - The primary market saw two sterling deals surface amid a dearth of supply ahead of the U.S. jobs data on Friday. BGB Finance Ireland set a 150 million pound Dec 2012 bond and Bank Austria set a 125 million pound Dec 1999 bond. St George Bank set a $500 million five-year FRN. In the mark sector, Sachsen Landesbank launched a 1.0 billion mark June 2002 bond while Depfa added 1.0 billion marks to its June 2004 bond.
